title: Mt Ololokwe road trip and hike tips
summary: Mount Ololokwe road trip through Samburu on the Marsabit road: real photos, hike time, guide and conservancy fees, and tips before you go.

posts.text: Ololokwe ni kama pilgrimage siku hizi, kila mtu na gari lazima afike. We took the Marsabit road through Samburu and yeah, this is a real place btw 🧵👇

image.alt: Mt Ololokwe's flat-topped cliffs at the end of the Isiolo–Marsabit highway, Samburu County, Kenya

posts.text: Early start is the move. Leave before dawn, fuel up kabla ya kutoka town because hutajua quality ya fuel huko mbele, and beat the heat.

posts.text: Ololokwe means "wide head" in Samburu, after the smooth rock on top. Locals also call it Ol Donyo Sabache, and it's a sacred mountain for the Samburu. Iko kama 350km from Nairobi, just past Archers Post.

posts.text: Road trip essentials: kinywaji baridi and Ololokwe kwa windscreen. Nothing else needed.

image.alt: Hand holding a cold drink in a plastic cup inside a car, Mt Ololokwe blurred behind

posts.text: Kama unataka kupanda: the hike is 3 to 5 hrs with a Samburu guide, on paths elephants made. Juu kuna mist forest, cedars, giant cycads, and the whole Samburu plains below you.
Budget: conservancy fee + guide, roughly KSh 1,000 to 2,000 each depending where you start (confirm before you go). Most people start at Sabache Camp. Anza mapema, by midday jua ni kali sana.
One more thing. Kuna watu wanaacha takataka huko. Please carry your litter back, hii mlima ni sacred kwa Samburu.
